screens.title: Medication administration record
screens.purpose: Checklist of scheduled doses; chart Administered/Held/Refused/Missed after the checks; PRN doses; the prepared dose's label.

tasks.summary: Clear a discharge stage (in order)
Medication Administration Record (checklist)
Chart a scheduled dose (Administered / Held / Refused / Missed)
Chart a PRN / ad-hoc dose
Correction entry for a charted dose
Generate scheduled doses from active IPD orders (idempotent)
Ward-local stock
Prepare a dose and print its label
The PRN orders a dose can be given from
Print a prepared dose's label again

rules: Clear the NursingMARVerification discharge stage from the ward once every due dose is charted and the patient's own medicines are handed back (OWN_MEDICINES_HELD lists them).

'Give' walks the rights (MSDS 64-68): 1) scan the wristband into wristband_code (no scanner: ask the name and the date of birth or MRN, identity_check TwoIdentifiers; an unidentified emergency patient: EmergencyOverride with identity_note); PATIENT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH: STOP, another patient's band. 2) scan the medicine into drug_barcode (DRUG_MISMATCH: STOP) or read its label. 3) the dose, route and time as ordered; anything else (or more than the time window) needs variance_reason (ADMINISTRATION_VARIANCE_REASON_REQUIRED).

A high-alert medicine (high_alert_category set: red badge; lasa_with: 'looks like …') needs a second nurse or doctor at the bedside: they check independently and type their username and password (second_checker_username/_password; HIGH_ALERT_CHECK_REQUIRED without). A nurse without a PNC registration cannot give doses (ADMINISTRATION_NOT_AUTHORIZED).
'Prepare' before drawing up an injection or infusion: POST /mar/{mar_id}/prepare (what it is diluted in) prints the label to stick on the syringe or bag before preparing the next one (MSDS 63).
self_administration lines: the patient takes it; chart it with self_administered true.
Anything other than Administered requires status_reason.
Doses given from ward stock: pass ward_stock_batch_id + qty (BATCH_EXPIRED, BATCH_RECALLED: take another batch).

'Give a PRN dose': pick the line from GET /admissions/{admission_id}/mar/prn-orders (the medicine, dose, route, interval_hours, instructions, last_given_at and given_last_24h: show them before giving), never a typed id; then the same rights as a scheduled dose, POST /admissions/{admission_id}/mar/prn with an Idempotency-Key. MEDICATION_ORDER_STOPPED: the order was stopped meanwhile, refresh the list.

'Reprint label' on a prepared dose (prepared_at set): GET /mar/{mar_id}/dose-label prints the recorded label again, marked REPRINT; never prepare the dose again to get a label, and never rebuild one on the terminal. DOSE_NOT_PREPARED: prepare it first.

tasks.summary: Consents still to take or to scan
The consent register
The situations that need a consent, with their forms
Who decides for a patient who cannot
Prepare a consent form
A consent
Edit a prepared consent
The consent form (A4)
The consent form as a PDF
Record a consent as given
Record an informed refusal
Withdraw a given consent
Cancel a prepared consent
Attach the scan of the signed form
Upload a patient document (PDF/JPEG/PNG)
Find a staff member for a form (badge facts only)

rules: Worklist first (GET /consent-worklist, `mine` for the caller's patients): the admissions without the general consent, the operations not signed in without their consents (OperationConsent, AnaesthesiaConsent), the signed forms still to scan; `overdue` in red; `consent_id` opens the draft already prepared.

Prepare: the form (GET /consent-forms) and the language the patient understands (only languages the form has; CONSENT_TEXT_MISSING lists details.available). POST /consents with the admission, the operation or the visit fills the patient and what it can (the procedure, the surgeon, the anaesthetist, the need for admission); complete what `missing` lists (the procedure, who performs it, risks, benefits, alternatives; for the general consent the need, the stay and the cost).

Print it (print-payload) and lay out `fields.consent.form_body` in `fields.consent.direction`: rtl (Urdu and the other languages but English) in a Nastaliq or Naskh font, `text` and `pdf_url` are then null. Explain it, read it aloud when the patient cannot read, have it signed or thumb-printed, with the witness.

Record the decision: Sign (signer Patient; or DecisionMaker, with a relationship GET /consent-decision-makers allows for this patient: an adult uses adult_priority, a child minor_priority, else CONSENT_SIGNER_INVALID; the questions and answers; a tick 'the patient explained it back'), or Refuse with the reason (VerbalRefusal: witnessed). In an emergency with nobody to consent: mode EmergencyNote, the note and the second doctor.

The caller is stamped as the professional who explained it: an informed consent needs a registered doctor, anaesthesia a doctor of the anaesthesia team (CONSENT_TAKER_NOT_AUTHORIZED). CONSENT_INCOMPLETE lists details.missing: mark those fields.

Scan the signed paper: upload it as a patient document of type Consent (POST /patients/{patient_id}/documents), then POST /consents/{consent_id}/scan. A decided consent is final: Withdraw it (with the reason) and take a new one. Refresh on consent.updated.

Who signs comes from the consent's who_decides, the server's own rule for this patient: patient_may_sign false (a minor by the hospital's adult_age) offers only a decision maker; offer who_decides.decision_makers in their order and no other relationship; ask for the second doctor of an EmergencyNote when emergency_second_doctor. Never classify the patient or hardcode an age of consent on the terminal.

screens.title: Blood transfusion at the bedside
screens.purpose: The units issued for the nurse's patients: the bedside check by two people, the start within 30 minutes of the issue, observations, the end, a reaction, or the unit sent back.
screens.workflow: Blood transfusion (decisions 43); the II C manual p155-157

tasks.summary: Blood requests
One blood request
One transfusion
Record observations during a transfusion
The bedside check by two people, then the start
End a transfusion
Report a transfusion reaction
Sign a unit back, or record it as not given
Scan to verify a patient's identity

rules: On blood.consent.withdrawn (critical): every unit of `units_out` must not be started; sign it back or record it as not given, and stop a transfusion that is running (BLOOD_CONSENT_REQUIRED at the start).

On blood.unit.issued show the unit with a countdown to start_by (30 minutes after the issue): after it the server refuses the start and the sign-back (BLOOD_UNIT_OUT_TOO_LONG); offer only 'Not given' with discard_reason OutOfStorageTooLong.

Start: scan the wristband (wristband_code) or confirm two identifiers; five checkboxes, none ticked in advance (identity on every document, unit number, expiry, product, bag); the second nurse or doctor types their username and password on the same screen (STEP_UP_REQUIRED, DUAL_CONTROL_SAME_PERSON). Any check that fails is not a start: open 'Not given' (POST /blood/transfusions/{transfusion_id}/return with fit_for_use false).
Observations: a baseline before the start, then as the ward takes them (no frequency is imposed). End: Completed, or Stopped with why; ended_late (more than 4 hours after the issue) shows in amber.

Reaction: the report on the manual's format creates its incident in the same call (show the incident number); wrong_blood reports the sentinel event. The form's type of reaction: reaction_class (DelayedHaemolytic asks delayed_after and the antibody, Bacterial the organism) and fatal (only with harm Death). BLOOD_REACTION_EXISTS: open the existing report.
Only while the blood_transfusion service is Active or Retiring for requests made before; history stays readable after.

tasks.summary: My practice deck: the question of the day and what to rehearse now

Record how well I knew a question (Knew, Partly, DidNotKnow)

A role's pocket guide as a print payload, in English or Urdu
Mock interviews, newest first (staff who do not conduct them see their own)

rules: Login card (every workspace, msds.interview.practice): `question_of_the_day` from GET .../my-deck with a 'Practise' button; hide it when null.

Flashcard: show the question (and, on 'Ask it differently', one of `variants`); the user answers aloud or in their head; 'Show the answer' reveals `model_answer`, then the `key_points` as a checklist; three buttons Knew / Partly / Didn't know → POST .../rehearsals; then the next card of `due`. Show `follow_ups` as 'The surveyor may ask next', `pitfalls` as 'Avoid', `show_me` as 'Be ready to show'.

The aim is that staff can explain what they actually do, as the hospital's SOPs say: never present the model answer as a script to memorise. Show under every answer: 'If a key point is not true on your ward, tell your in-charge: it is a gap to fix, not a line to learn.' (the answer's `notice`, in its language)
Facts: values from the hospital's settings are already filled in `model_answer`; a fact with `set` false shows as a bracketed prompt: never invent a value.
Badges: the PHC type (Mandatory red, Operational yellow, always with its word), the indicator number in the hospital's category (`indicators_in_category`), 'Adapted to our SOP' when `adapted`.
Progress (GET .../my-progress): ready %, the streak, per chapter knew / partly / not known / not rehearsed; the last mock interview with its score (open it: GET .../mock-interviews/{id}).

Browse all (GET .../questions?mine=true, then any role) and 'Print my pocket guide': in English GET .../pocket-guide/pdf (a PDF: one click, one file); in Urdu GET .../pocket-guide?lang=ur, laid out by the app right to left and printed from the terminal (the server's PDFs are Latin script only).
INTERVIEW_QUESTION_NOT_APPLICABLE: the hospital took the question out; drop the card and refresh the deck.

Language (the vendor's request of 2026-10-09): send `lang` (en or ur) or rely on the user's preference (PUT /settings/me language); every answer says its `lang`, so offer an English / اردو switch on every card. Urdu (`direction` rtl): lay the texts out right to left in Noto Nastaliq Urdu (bundled in the app); medicine names, test names and the hospital's own records inside stay in English as typed. `text_status` Draft: show 'Draft translation' beside the answer until the vendor's native-speaker review; `question_en` gives the English wording a surveyor may use.
